messages.subject: A Speed question
parts:
ggplot2 friends,

sorry this question isn't exactly a ggplot specfic question but I am going to be using a rather large "while" loop in R and for each iteration generate a plot (using qplot) and saving it.  Does anyone know if this is quicker using R CMD through windows command line terminal vs. using the GUI or are they approximately the same.  Sorry if question does not meet the criteria of questions for this group.  Thank you ahead of time.

Best,
Brian

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: A Speed question
parts:
I don't think there would be much difference. Though you didn't ask,
for big gains, you might want to think in terms of partitioning the work
and running some things in parallel (assuming you have the resources
available). Then you have to think about memory consumption and
swapping. Then you'll want to consider the density of the data you are
using and whether or not you can get the same graphs with fewer data
points. For example, if you are interpolating on a very dense grid, ask
yourself if the grid is much denser than the output plot will be. If
you can shrink the data, the serial and the parallel processing will be
much faster, and you will have less of an issue with thrashing memory.
Also make sure you don't grow memory use by accumulating a bunch of
objects that just hang around when you are done with them.

Hope this isn't too much pontification!

Mark

messages.subject: Re: A Speed question
parts:
I often deal with this problem, and I use sflapply (package:snowfall)
to do the loop in parallel. Thisis especially effective if you are
saving as opposed to rendering the plots on a graphics device. If you
are actually rendering the plots, ggplot usually takes more time to
make the plots than you can save by making them in parallel.
